title: Beta Rollforward Checklist and KPI Escape Plan
body:
Purpose:
This document defines the operational checklist for a controlled beta rollforward and an explicit KPI-driven escape plan (rollforward -> stabilize or execute escape actions). It is intended for product ops, SRE, serving-runtime, and solutions engineering. Use as the canonical on-the-day playbook and the post-beta postmortem input source.

Scope:
- Beta cohort: internal + invited external customers (~500 daily active sessions)
- Surface areas: Hosted API route /v1/beta-chat and related embedding endpoints
- Timebox: 14-day rolling beta followed by phased ramp to GA

Success criteria (primary KPIs and thresholds):
- Availability (user-facing): >= 99.5% per day.
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 750ms for baseline sequences (<= 2s for long sequences).
- Error rate: 5xxs + application errors <= 0.8% of requests per hour.
- Quality regression: hallucination rate on canned prompts <= baseline + 2ppt (measured by eval suite).
- Cost: average token-unit cost per 1k requests must be within target budget (<= $X per 1k; ops to confirm).
- Adoption/engagement: retention at 7 days >= 20% for invited cohort.

Pre-launch readiness checks (T-72h):
- Confirm capacity commit: Dedicated pool reserved for beta (infra lead).
- Load test: running 3x projected concurrency with KV-cache patterns (SRE).
- Canary traffic: successful canary for model variant and routing policy for 48h.
- Alerting: dashboards wired (latency, error-rate, token-cost, model-quality signal).
- Backfill prompts: golden prompt set uploaded and smoke eval passing.
- Support plan: CS on call roster + pre-written customer-facing message templates.

Go / No-Go gates (T-2h):
- All critical alerts green for 24h.
- Canary error rate <= 0.5% and p95 <= 750ms.
- Escalation contacts verified and reachable.
- All feature flags and model-variant fallbacks validated.

Traffic-mitigation recipes (escape actions ordered by disruption -> speed):
1) Throttle upstream traffic (rate limits by API key tier) — low-risk immediate relief.
2) Reduce concurrency per worker / reduce batch depth (runtime config flip) — reduces tail latency at cost of throughput.
3) Switch traffic to lower-cost-compatible model variant (e.g., 8-bit quantized variant) with explicit quality-tolerance check — medium-risk.
4) Enable prefix/KV cache-only mode for returning sessions (degrades freshness but preserves UX) — medium-risk.
5) Route portion of traffic to Dedicated burst capacity regionally (if available) — requires infra approval.
6) Graceful degrade UX: switch to cached responses / shorter summaries and display notice to users — high-user-impact, last-resort.
7) Full rollback to pre-beta baseline (traffic cutover to previous model and config) — executed only after owner signoff.

Decision triggers (examples):
- Immediate trigger: 5xx rate > 1.5% sustained for 10 minutes OR p95 > 1200ms for 15 minutes.
- Near-term trigger: Cost per 1k requests > target by 30% sustained for 2 hours.
- Quality trigger: hallucination regression > 4ppt on eval prompts OR customer escalations > 3 in 1 hour.

Concrete runbook (who does what):
- Product Ops Lead (Maya Thompson): decision authority for rollforward vs escape; coordinate cross-team communications.
- SRE Lead (Ethan Park): execute throttles, adjust runtime concurrency, monitor infra alarms.
- Serving Runtime (Jordan Lee): flip model-variant routing, implement cache-mode toggles, confirm KV cache health.
- Solutions Eng / CS (Sofia Martinez): customer comms, triage priority tickets, collect example failures for model team.
- Infra Lead (Priya Rao): enable burst capacity / region shifts; validate network and capacity prerequisites.

Escalation matrix and contact channels:
- Slack channel: #beta-rollforward (primary)
- Pager: SRE on-call (PagerDuty) -> phone if not acknowledged in 5m
- Exec escalation: VP Product -> VP Engineering if decision to rollback likely

On-day timeline (condensed):
- T-2h: Final canary check, stakeholders standup, confirm analytics ingestion
- T0: Enable beta routing for 5% of cohort traffic (monitor live)
- T+30m: expand to 25% if flat; validate KPIs at 25m and 60m
- T+2h: expand to 50% if stable; otherwise execute mitigation recipe #1 or #2
- T+6h: evaluate quality signals and customer feedback; decision checkpoint for next 24h cadence

Communication templates (short):
- Customer-facing: "We're running a limited beta for X feature. You may see intermittent differences; we're monitoring closely and will update in-channel. Report issues to support@redwood.com."
- Internal incident: "[BETA:ALERT] KPI breach detected: {metric} at {value}. Executing mitigation step {n}. Leads: @mthompson @epark"

Post-escape stabilization checklist (after mitigation/rollback):
- Confirm baseline KPIs restored for 2h after action.
- Collect 100+ examples of failure cases for model and infra postmortem.
- Run targeted test harness against flagged prompts.
- Recreate incident in staging if possible and file follow-up Jira with RCA owner.
- Customer outreach: send personalized notes to affected beta customers and offer support credits where appropriate.

Post-beta evaluation (within 7 days):
- Full KPI deck: availability, latency, error-rate, cost, quality regressions, engagement metrics.
- Lessons learned: 3 operational changes to prevent recurrence, 2 product changes, 1 infra investment (priority-ranked).
- Rollout recommendation: proceed/graduate with phased GA or iterate on beta for X weeks.

Notes, open questions, and TODOs:
- Need to finalize cost-per-1k target with finance (Finance ticket FIN-2025-72).
- Confirm whether Dedicated burst is charged to Beta budget or infra overhead.
- Add synthetic user simulator for long-tail prompts in nightly cron.

Appendix: Example Jira tasks to pre-create (short labels):
- PROD-BETA-001: throttle rate-limit implementation by API tier
- PROD-BETA-002: model-variant routing toggle + fallback test
- PROD-BETA-003: customer incident template and CS playbook

Document owner: Maya Thompson (product-ops). Keep this doc as the single source for day-of run decisions and checklist entries.

Revision log:
- 2025-09-12: initial draft
- 2025-09-15: added traffic-mitigation recipes and decision triggers (SRE review)
- 2025-09-18: updated timeline and contact roster after dry-run
